component.name: Badge
component.description: Small, non-interactive text label that tags content with a short category or status (e.g. a course topic such as 'Design'). Text only — no icon, not clickable, not focusable. Two looks: outlined (default, border only) and filled (subtle tinted background).

when: Tagging a course or item with its topic or category (e.g. 'Design', 'Design Thinking')
Showing a short, static status next to content where no action is expected

patterns.name: topic-list
patterns.description: A wrapping row of Badges listing an item's topics, placed next to the content it tags (e.g. under a course title). The surrounding heading or text provides context; the badges are read in order.

antiPatterns.scenario: Making a Badge clickable (onClick, href, tabIndex) to filter by its topic
antiPatterns.reason: Badge is a static label: it renders a <span>, has no focus or hover state, and its props type omits onClick/role/tabIndex.
antiPatterns.alternative: Use Chip for a filter toggle, or TextLink / Button for navigation and actions.

antiPatterns.scenario: Adding an icon or long sentence inside a Badge
antiPatterns.reason: Badge is text-only and does not wrap (white-space: nowrap); long content breaks the row layout.
antiPatterns.alternative: Keep the label to one to three words. Use Text for longer descriptive content.

antiPatterns.scenario: Overriding the label colour or typography via className or a nested Text
antiPatterns.reason: The label is always rendered by Badge through Text size=body-default color=subtle; pass a plain string as children.
antiPatterns.alternative: Choose variant=outlined or variant=filled; never wrap children in another Text or Heading.

purpose.outlined: Default look. Transparent background with the default border.
purpose.filled: Subtle tinted background with a stronger border, for slightly more emphasis or contrast against a busy surface.

states.description: Static label — no interaction, lifecycle, or content fallback states.

accessibility.notes: Renders a plain <span>; the label text is read in reading order. Not focusable. Place badges next to the content they tag so the context is clear in reading order.
